summary: ProcessTelegramUpdateJob faithfully implements Decisions 5, 9, and 12. The re-entry guard is the first action after load (no event/stub/counter on DONE), cascade ordering puts every logEventBlocking(...).block() before the rawUpdate save, the failure handler is atomic (findAndModify), scrubs+truncates correctly, increments the failure counter, and rethrows so JobRunr retries. The atomic ownerChatId populate uses the exact (_id, status=CONNECTED, ownerChatId=null) predicate per Decision 5. Dispatch matrix matches the task's enumeration including edge cases (bot==null, media-only message, channel posts without sender). Tests exercise all enumerated ACs and the re-entry path. Suggestions are minor (test gap for /stop in group, no behavioural assertion for cascade ordering, no INFO worker-start/completion log).

suggestions.suggestion: Add a `/stop` in group/supergroup test case symmetric to startGroup_eventOnly_noStubsNoOwnerPopulate. The implementation routes group /stop through handleStop and emits telegram_command_stop without calling stubs, but this behaviour is not explicitly enumerated in the task's Step-3 matrix and has zero test coverage — a future refactor could quietly change the classification (event_other vs command_stop) without breaking a test.
suggestions.benefit: Locks in the (currently undocumented) group-/stop classification and protects against silent regression.

suggestions.suggestion: There is no test that directly proves Decision-12 cascade ordering (event-write must complete BEFORE save(processingStatus=DONE)). The task line 110 explicitly says "Verified by reading the source ordering AND by unit-test in T9 if practical." One way: stub rawUpdateRepository.save to throw, invoke worker, and assert (a) the event still landed in events collection, (b) rawUpdate is then marked FAILED by the catch handler. Without this, a reordered refactor would only be caught by code review.
suggestions.benefit: Mechanises the audit-survival invariant ("no DONE row without its audit event") so it cannot be silently violated.

suggestions.suggestion: Tech-spec Risks → Token-scrubber sites enumerates five worker log sites (INFO worker start, WARN per-command branches with chatId+scrubbed payload, ERROR terminal failure, INFO ownerChatId populate, INFO worker success). Implementation has only two (ERROR failure + INFO populate). The omitted sites are NOT required by ACs, but their absence makes the success path opaque in production — operator can only confirm "the worker ran" via the success counter, not via log correlation. Consider mirroring ProjectHardDeleteJob's "run completed" INFO line at minimum (scrubbed rawUpdateId + updateKind + projectId + durationMs).
suggestions.benefit: Closes the operational visibility gap that motivated the original tech-spec enumeration, without changing AC behaviour.

suggestions.suggestion: logEventOther uses HashMap while logEventCommandStart/Stop/MessageReceived use LinkedHashMap. The functional difference is iteration order (LinkedHashMap preserves insertion, HashMap does not), which matters for log/audit readability when the metadata is later printed or serialised. Use LinkedHashMap consistently across all four helpers — the in-method comment on line 247 already calls out the choice.
suggestions.benefit: Consistent metadata field ordering across all event types in the audit log and in any future log line that prints the Map.

suggestions.suggestion: Bot is looked up via botRepository.findByProjectIdAndStatus three times per worker invocation for /start, /stop, and plain-text-private paths (lines 171, 196, 234). All three branches need the same bot for the same projectId. Hoist a single lookup at the top of dispatch (after the message != null gate) and pass it as a parameter to handleStart/handleStop/plainTextPrivate. Saves two Mongo round-trips on every text message and eliminates the three duplicate "bot == null → log unknown" branches.
suggestions.benefit: ~2x fewer Mongo reads on the hot path; collapses repeated null-bot handling into one place.
